items.desc: In a complaint filed through his wife, Sapkota claims he was blindfolded after being detained at the airport, held at an undisclosed location, forced to give statements against prominent figures and subjected to mental torture.

items.title: Balendra Shah’s India trip: From nationalist posturing to realpolitik
items.desc: Delhi’s warm welcome and a slew of agreements signal an important opening in ties. But translating diplomatic goodwill into tangible outcomes will take more than one visit.

items.title: Home Minister Sudan Gurung to hold traditional wedding in Gorkha
items.desc: Prime Minister Balendra Shah and Rastriya Swatantra Party chairman Rabi Lamichhane are expected to attend the ceremony on December 3, which is also intended to promote the village as a wedding destination.

items.title: Embassy’s refusal stalls Supreme Court ruling on video testimony from abroad
items.desc: A landmark ruling allowing accused persons overseas to testify remotely remains unimplemented after Nepali embassy in Australia says it has neither authority nor the facilities to enforce the court order.

items.title: Court remands former chief secretary Aryal for four days
items.desc: Ek Narayan Aryal is being investigated over alleged fraud and organised crime linked to extra biomedical fees charged to Nepali workers seeking jobs in Malaysia.

items.title: Trump says he asked Putin to ‘pull back’ military aggression throughout Europe
items.desc: Trump did not ​elaborate on what conduct he was asking Putin to halt. Since the Russian invasion of Ukraine started in 2022, other countries have occasionally accused Russia of provocative behaviour.

items.title: Bhotekoshi flood victims may get up to Rs800,000 for new homes
items.desc: The government plans to provide one-time housing grants based on geographical regions, while families who lost their land will be included in an integrated housing programme.

items.title: Mahakali bridge opens, ending years of risky river crossings
items.desc: Jointly inaugurated by Prime Ministers Balendra Shah and Narendra Modi, the bridge replaces risky cable and inner-tube crossings between Nepal and India.

items.title: Displaced families protest as Bode holding centre faces eviction deadline
items.desc: Residents banged plates after receiving no food by noon, hours before the government’s 2pm deadline to vacate the centre.

items.title: Rabi Lamichhane meets President Paudel
items.desc: Talks at Sheetal Niwas covered the government, parliament, ordinances and current political developments, according to Lamichhane’s secretariat.

items.title: Army storm into women’s cricket semifinals with 97-run win over Karnali
items.desc: Karnali crash out of the 10th National Games after suffering their second consecutive defeat. Samjhana Khadka stars with a halfcentury.

items.title: Human Rights Watch urges Nepal to act against illegal moneylenders
items.desc: The rights watchdog says Gulf conflict-related disruptions have left migrant workers unable to repay high-interest loans, exposing families to threats, violence, forced evictions and sexual exploitation.

items.title: TU steps up efforts to reclaim encroached land, gives occupants seven days
items.desc: The university has warned of forced eviction with government assistance as the latest deadline for unauthorised occupants nears expiry.

items.title: 12 arrested over gambling at Birgunj casino
items.desc: Nine were caught gambling at Fortune City Gaming Club, while three others were accused of allowing Nepali citizens to enter the casino and facilitating gambling.

items.title: Residents threaten to shut Mahakali bridge over delay in rebuilding suspension bridge
items.desc: The bridge linking Dodhara Chandani to the rest of Kanchanpur was severed by floods two months ago, disrupting daily life and hitting local businesses.

items.title: After virtual idols, could fully AI-generated stars be K-pop’s next frontier?
items.desc: Synthetic acts such as Seoria, H3arus test whether K-pop fandom can form around idols with no human performer behind the character.

items.title: Parties gear up for local elections despite no date being set
items.desc: The RSP has opened applications through its Candidate Club, while the Congress plans primaries and the UML and NCP focus on strengthening their organisations.

items.title: Where the August floods began
items.desc: A massive ice and rock avalanche from Langtang Lirung plunged into the Lhende river on August 26, triggering devastating floods that swept through Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading.

items.title: Telecom regulator and operators face minister’s ire over poor service
items.desc: Communications Minister Bikram Timilsina warns of action against service providers that fail to meet licence conditions, and questions the need for a regulator unable to hold them accountable.

items.title: Musk pledges two SpaceX shares for every US child in $18 billion AI charm offensive
items.desc: Musk says the giveaway will give every US child two shares in the space company, worth nearly $18 billion in total, as SpaceX expands into AI and faces growing scrutiny over its plans for space-based data centres.

items.title: Footballers find hope in Surkhet as 10th National Games ends a long drought
items.desc: After years of league stagnation and federation turmoil, players across seven provinces and three departmental teams find a vital competitive stage in Surkhet.

items.title: Three months on, flood survivors still await government response
items.desc: With no resettlement plan, delayed rental assistance and relief running out, survivors face winter without secure shelter as aid organisations begin to withdraw.

items.title: After ex-ministers, ex-chief secretary arrested over Malaysia labour deal
items.desc: A police investigation into an eight-year-old labour agreement between Nepal and Malaysia has halted the departure of Nepali workers for jobs in Malaysia. Thousands of workers have been unable to travel since October 1.

items.title: Who is responsible for Kathmandu’s evicted squatters?
items.desc: Seven months after the bulldozers, the state has found time for eviction notices but not for dialysis, decent meals or land certificates.

items.title: Sonia’s memoir: Bold, raw and a tad dishonest
items.desc: Even as the book glows with rawness and intrepidity in Sonia Gandhi’s personal thoughts, her lack of honest reflection on key political matters dims the shine.

items.title: How Delhi's grand diplomacy distracts us from the ongoing territorial occupation of Nepali land
items.desc: Kalapani is not a “boundary issue.” It is our land under illegal occupation. Until we state this clearly, we will continue to be misled.
